triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a rename or as pure generalization and could not: `entry_is_line_a` splits into two different predicates in different formulas (`entry_is_china_301_list123` in the §301 component, `entry_is_section_122_exempt` in the §122 component) and `entry_is_line_b` splits three ways (`entry_is_china_301_2024_action`, `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, `entry_is_section_232_covered`), while both flags survive elsewhere in the post file (lines 1907, 1924, 2367, 2523) — a rename cannot do that, so encoded meaning changed. The pre-fix summary states the flags are "caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification", so at chapter scale the old gate zeroed the 10% surcharge for any ch37 line classified as a China-301 list-1 / 2024-action member, which the cited source never authorizes: Proclamation 11012 ¶14 enumerates the exceptions (Annex II list, "(k) all articles and parts of articles currently or that later become subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232", USMCA/CAFTA-DR, etc.) with no §301-membership carve-out, and the rule's own unchanged exception atoms cite the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) list and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper ... provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04". The fix therefore re-grounds a branch condition that had no basis in the cited provision — untraceable_branch, not amount, boundary, period, or inverted logic.
